text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: router.p99 > 1.2s in us-west (streaming) — auto-page to #incidents. trace_id=abc123

lina: saw the alert, joining. p99 spike started ~1845006700 per dashboards, p95 up ~200ms too.

chris: I'm oncall. quick check: is this isolated to streaming endpoints or all generation?

lina: streaming endpoints, especially long-sequence sessions (>1k tokens). non-streaming endpoints seem okay.

rajesh: adding stats: we see a bumped tail on router->modelpool handoffs. error rate still low, just latency. heatmap shows a handful of pods at 96-99th percentile.

matt: any recent deploys to routing policy or LB config in us-west in the last hour?

lina: yes, there was a routing policy tweak 30m ago to change weight for v2 fallback policy (experiment to prefer cheaper variant). I flagged it in the config-prs channel but forgot to mention potential hotkey effects.

chris: can you paste the policy revision id?

lina: policy revision r5678. snippet: ```json
{"route_rules": [{"matcher": "prefix:/stream", "weights": {"v1": 0.2, "v2": 0.8}}]}```

rajesh: that aligns. v2 is on a smaller scaled pool and has a KV cache warm-up behavior that stalls when a hot partition hits it. Looks like a few hotkeys are being routed to that smaller pool now.

chris: OK — this looks like a misrouting-induced hot-partition causing tail stalls. Impact: external customers using streaming might see stalls and partial streams. Severity: Sev2 currently. Who can roll back policy quickly?

lina: I can roll back to r5677 (previous weights) now. Rolling in 30s.

support-bot: Notifying customers tagged as "streaming-alpha" with a short banner: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls in us-west. Minimal impact. Update soon."

matt: hold off one sec — before rollback let's try an emergency mitigation that's less disruptive: temporarily increase v2 pool capacity and add an explicit hotkey blackhole rule for the top offenders. That way we avoid global rollback if we can patch routing.

chris: good call. lina, can you patch routing table to add a rule: top-keys -> force v1? Or add a blacklist to v2 for top keys?

lina: I can add a temporary matcher for the hotkeys. Need the list. Rajesh — can you surface top 10 keys?

rajesh: pulling aggregated router logs... top keys: user:acct:7685, user:acct:1129, convo:bot:33, convo:bot:33 (duplicate due to sessions), user:acct:4423, model:chat:freq-7, user:acct:9991, convo:bot:12, user:acct:223, user:acct:8802.

matt: recommend blackholing those to v1 for 10m and spin v2 up +2 replicas. lina, if rollback is faster do it, but try blackhole+scale first.

lina: applying patch now. Patching router policy: ```bash
curl -XPOST $ROUTER_API/policies/rules -d '{"matcher":"key_contains:user:acct:|convo:bot:","force_route":"v1","ttl":600}'
```

lina: patch applied. Verifying...

rajesh: logs show immediate drop in p99 for those flows. cluster v2 pods still showing high latency for other keys, but overall p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 480ms.

chris: good. lina, please also scale v2 by +2 replicas; matt can you authorize?

matt: authorizing scale. running kscale: ```bash
kubectl scale deploy v2-pool --replicas=6 -n inference-us-west
```

oncall-bot: Scaling event queued by matt. Estimated 90s to readiness.

lina: rollback still an option if this doesn't stabilize.

rajesh: after blackhole+scale p95 ~120ms, p99 ~480ms, streaming stalls largely mitigated. Some lingering stalls at very long sessions, likely due to KV cache thrash.

chris: status update to exec: "mitigation applied (hotkey reroute + scale), p99 reduced ~60%, monitoring." Lina, can you post a short timeline of actions? Also assign a follow-up incident for root cause analysis and policy safety.

lina: timeline: 1845006700 alert -> 1845006789 pager -> 1845006820 identified routing policy change r5678 -> 1845006880 applied hotkey patch -> 1845006935 scaled v2 -> 1845007060 p99 dropped to ~480ms. I'll open a ticket: INC-2026-1845-RoutingHotkey

support-bot: Customer banner updated to: "Issue mitigated. Some customers may have seen delayed streaming responses in us-west between 18:11-18:21 UTC. We continue to monitor."

matt: can we mark as "mitigated" and continue monitoring for 30m?

chris: yes. leaving oncall to monitor. Lina take postmortem owner. Rajesh, add relevant traces and heatmaps to the ticket.

rajesh: will export traces and attach slow-sql-like KV lookups and hop latencies. Suspect pattern: routing weight change caused traffic shift to a smaller pool with uneven key hotspots -> cache miss storms -> backend stalls for streaming.

lina: taking postmortem. immediate next steps: 1) rollback permanent policy until safety checks done, 2) add automated guardrails on routing weight changes to prevent routing >50% to smaller pools without gradual canary, 3) add hotkey detector alert that triggers before route shifts take effect.

chris: also add a circuit-breaker in routing that enforces per-pod qps threshold and fallbacks when a pod's 95th jumps >X.

matt: I'll sync with product on policy UI to show pool capacity and instance counts next to weight sliders.

oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Pager cleared.

lina: closing thread here, updating INC-2026-1845-RoutingHotkey with logs and next steps. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

chris: nice quick mitigation. please include customer impact summary in the ticket (est. 18:11-18:21 UTC, us-west streaming p99 elevated, small % of customers affected).

support-bot: Customer follow-up scheduled: email to "streaming-alpha" cohort in 1h with details.

lina: last note — we should run a canary on the policy change pipeline so future weight changes are rolled out to 2% of traffic first. I'll add to the postmortem action list.

chris: agreed. switching to monitoring.
